answer: A dry-stone wall segment on a knoll is the price of one identity. The builder locks an 80-credit bond in the vault and spends 40 credits on stone, 120 per identity, and the segment enters a public plan keyed to the builder. A falcon auditor re-measures its length and height against that plan; a shortfall forfeits the bond. Each further fake buys a fresh segment, bond and stone, so 1,000 fakes run to 120,000 credits, each priced alone, while a single honest builder spends 120. A rented wall fails: that segment is already entered in the plan, so the second claim forfeits both bonds.
